allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: mid-green leaves; blue-purple flowers.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.note: The leaf drawn as a palmately compound leaf (spec rework P4), its leaflets counted and set from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants; before, a palmately lobed blade stood in for it. By eye from photographs: the leaflets fanned nearly all the way round the petiole's tip (300 degrees), the outer ones 0.6 as long as the middle one, each oblanceolate, tapering to its foot, and about a sixth as wide as long.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.leaflets.note: How PlantGen draws a divided leaf, a choice of the model's (spec rework P4): the leaf characters set a compound card's pattern, its leaflets or pinnae, the leaflets on each pinna, and whether its segments run together. A pinnate leaf's count says how it ends (odd-pinnate odd, even-pinnate even), so a flora's range is drawn as the nearest count of the right kind.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its raceme drawn as one cluster that opens by the day (spec rework L1c), its kind from its characters, by the rule at the flowering plants, where before the herb placed flowers, buds and pods along the stem by their place, whatever the day: 100 flowers in whorls of four (Pohtio and Teras found 100 to 200 on naturalised plants in Finland; no flora gives a count), on a raceme about 38 cm long above a 7 cm peduncle, pedicels about 8 mm, each flower about 14 mm, blue-purple with a pale banner patch, from purple buds, and pods 3.5 cm after. From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. The plant stands as tall as before: its stems end where the peduncle begins.

appearance.organs.flower.inflorescence.k.note: How PlantGen lays out an inflorescence, a choice of the model's (spec rework L1): the inflorescence characters set the cluster of any look a taxon draws as one (`"inflorescence": {}`), its kind, how many units it bears on each axis, its primary branches and how it holds itself. Sizes, stalks and spacing stay set by hand until programs size their organs from characters.

appearance.organs.flower.season.note: Its days by eye from the months floras and guides give for flowering (the Burke Herbarium: June to September; Minnesota Wildflowers: May to July), for lowland plants: buds in late May, each flower open about 12 days, the raceme opening from its foot (as the Wisconsin DNR describes) over about four weeks (no source gives a time), its pods shed by early September.

appearance.organs.flower.season.flower_l.note: Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5): its petals, sepals, banner, wings and keel, stamens and pistil set from the characters of Fabaceae and Lupinus by the rules at the flowering plants. Its calyx by hand from VicFlora and the Flora of New Zealand, as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): 5 to 10 mm against a corolla of 12 to 20 mm, 2-lipped, its lobes longer than its tube.

The rules also set these fields in a season's flower and bud looks that draw a flower, unless set there by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a tall lupine with palmate leaves of nine to seventeen leaflets and dense spires of blue-purple pea flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.basal_length.note: How the herb program draws a palmate leaf from a flora's petiole and leaflet lengths, a choice of the model's (spec rework E4): its card is the petiole and a leaflet end to end, so the leaf is as long as both and the petiole's share is its length over theirs.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): the sexual system its taxa state most often decides; a species whose taxa state dioecy no more often than another system bears both sexes on every plant until it states its own.

generator.params.leaf_length.note: How the herb program draws a palmate leaf from a flora's petiole and leaflet lengths, a choice of the model's (spec rework E4): its card is the petiole and a leaflet end to end, so the leaf is as long as both and the petiole's share is its length over theirs.

generator.params.leaf_top.note: Its leaves are few and all long-stalked, on petioles 15 to 30 cm (Abrams vol. 2, 1944, p. 515), so the topmost stem leaf is drawn 0.7 as long as the longest, by hand: no flora gives how they shrink up the stem.

generator.params.leaves_per_node.note: What the words mean, as accounts of phyllotaxis such as Okabe and colleagues' use them: a spiral or two-ranked shoot bears one leaf at a node, a decussate one a pair and a whorled one three or more. A spiral turns about the golden angle (137.5 degrees) from node to node and two ranks half a turn; pairs and whorls alternate, each standing over the gaps of the one below, half the gap between its own leaves round (90 degrees for pairs). Three ranks turn a third of a turn, as their name says.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
